label: Captain Holt, late runs — the record in monotone

purpose.value: Holt delivers the after-action record in parade-ground monotone: nothing has ever crossed the gates but the hero, every battle still starts at his border crossing, and the people he fights now drill being afraid of him.

emotionalProgression.note: No more reviews, just the record, delivered flat so nothing in it can be mistaken for rhetoric.
'Evacuation drills now. When your amulet glows. That's the enemy you're fighting — people who practice being afraid of you.'

notes: The escalation endpoint for the border arc: professional detachment has cracked; the flatness is the feeling. Late dialogue may also name what the trophy mechanic is (he knows the full Heavy Hands / gate-seal chain): stripping badges off stretcher-bearers. The last honest attempt. The hero's reply will still be some variant of 'At last, the enemy respects me.' — that framing belongs to his side of the exchange (notes only), never to an NPC line. Never validate the hero's prophecy framing: there is no canon fact supporting 'the realms are evil', and that absence is itself the guard.
